title: China's First Bank Was Born Here in 1823 — Pingyao, Shanxi | China Travel Expert
description:
Long before ATMs, one walled town in Shanxi invented a way to move money across China without carrying a single coin.

Pingyao is one of the best-preserved Ming and Qing county towns in China. In 1823 it gave birth to Rishengchang, China's first draft bank (piaohao): you could deposit silver in one city and cash a paper draft in another, hundreds of miles away. At its peak it ran 57 branches across 35 cities, with business reaching Europe and Southeast Asia — earning the name "the bank that connects the world." The whole town is still ringed by a Ming-dynasty wall over six kilometres long, cannon scars and all, wrapped around grey courtyards and old shopfronts. UNESCO listed it in 1997.

🧭 Expert Tip: Walk the full city wall at dawn before the tour groups arrive — you get the ramparts, the rooftops and the morning light almost to yourself.
